subject: A gray tabby cat curled up asleep on a folded yellow knitted blanket, on a wooden windowsill beside a sunny window, with a soft blue wall behind
focal_point: The cat's sleeping face at the left end of the curl: the closed eyes, the pink nose, the white muzzle and whiskers, and the two white paws tucked under the chin
light: Daylight comes through the window at the upper left. It lights the top and left side of the cat's head and back, the tops of the blanket's rolls, and lays slanted patches of peach sunlight on the sill at the left; the right side and underside of the cat and the right end of the blanket fall into shadow.
why: We work back to front: the bright window view first, then the blue wall and the window frame, then the sill, then the blanket the cat lies on, so the cat goes on last over finished surroundings. The cat gets the most steps, built the way a teacher builds an animal (shape, shadow, white patches, stripes, fur, face), and the face is saved for the very end so the lesson finishes at the focal point.

things.name: The sky and trees through the window
things.why: The sky seen through the glass is a smooth pale blue going whiter lower down, blended wet in one go behind the trees and the frame.

things.name: The leafy trees outside the window
things.why: A far tree mass seen through the glass: dabbed dark first, then sunlit leaves on top.
things.left_out: The middle green pass: these trees are far background in a small window, so two values (dark teal and sunny yellow-green) are enough, with no texture beyond the dabs.

things.name: The blue wall
things.why: The wall is one flat background going smoothly from pale periwinkle near the window to a deeper periwinkle on the right, blended wet in one go straight through where the cat and blanket will go.

things.name: The white window frame
things.why: A frame built from simple straight pieces (the upright post, the crossbar, the low ledge), then shaded on the sides turned away from the light.
things.left_out: A separate light pass: the frame's base is already the lightest color on it, so it gets a base and its lavender shadows only.

things.name: The wooden windowsill
things.why: A flat slab built from a rectangle for the top and a strip for the front edge, shaded and then lit with the sun patches. Shaped-object has no horizontal wood-grain stroke, so the pieces are laid as long straight strips along the sill instead.
things.left_out: Wood grain and the sill's corner joints.

things.name: The yellow knitted blanket
things.why: A thick folded blanket built from a flat oval ring and two long rolls in front, shaded in its folds, then given its knit texture as two passes of small comma stitches, dark then light.
things.left_out: Real knit structure: the stitches are suggested with rows of small press-and-lift commas following each roll, not knitted row by row.

things.name: The sleeping tabby cat
things.why: A short-haired tabby with dark stripes and white patches: exactly what this element builds, from the big curled shape to the face last.
things.left_out: The tufts of fur inside the ears, the brownish tint on the far ear, separate toe pads, and the fine whiskers above the eyes; the curled cat is kept to big pieces, bold stripes and short fur flicks.

steps.name: Blend the sky in the window

lays.what: the sky seen through the glass in the upper left: pale sky blue at the top, going to almost white lower down, run straight past where the trees and the frame bars will go

steps.after: The upper-left corner of the canvas is a smooth light-blue sky, bluer at the top and nearly white lower down, running a little past where the window's edges will be. The rest of the canvas is bare white.
steps.why: The view out of the window is the farthest thing in the picture, so it goes on first.

steps.name: Dab the dark leaves outside

lays.what: loose clumps of dark leaves in the window: a mass down the left edge and lower half of the window, and a clump at the top, with sky showing in gaps between them

steps.after: Dark teal-green dappled clumps of leaves fill the lower and left parts of the window sky and a smaller clump at its top, with pale sky showing between them. Everything outside the window is still bare white.

steps.name: Dab the sunlit leaves outside

lays.what: bright taps of light leaves on the upper and right sides of each dark clump, toward the light, leaving the dark teal showing underneath and below

steps.after: The trees in the window now have bright yellow-green tops and edges over the dark teal, which still shows in the lower and inner parts of each clump. The window view is finished; the rest of the canvas is bare white.

stages.name: The wall and the window frame

steps.name: Blend the blue wall

lays.what: the whole wall to the right of the window and down to the sill line: pale periwinkle near the window, deepening to soft periwinkle toward the right and lower down, straight through where the cat and blanket will lie

steps.after: Everything right of the window, from the top edge down to about two thirds of the way down, is a soft gray-blue wall, lighter near the window and deeper on the right, with no gap left for the cat. The window view sits at the upper left; the bottom third and the strip below the window are still bare white.

steps.name: Build the window frame from strips

lays.what: the frame from simple straight pieces: the upright post on the right side of the window, the thin crossbar across the glass, the edge of the frame at the far left, and the wide low ledge under the window down to the sill

steps.after: A creamy white window frame now surrounds the view: a wide upright post on its right, a thin crossbar across the trees, and a broad pale ledge below the window down to where the sill will be. It is flat cream with no shading yet; the wall and window view are as before, and the bottom of the canvas is bare.

steps.name: Shade the frame's shady sides

lays.what: soft lavender along the underside of the crossbar, the edges of the post, and a few lines on the ledge; deep blue-violet down the wide inner side of the window opening between the post and the wall

steps.after: The frame now looks like real wood with depth: lavender shadow lines under the crossbar and along the post and ledge, and a deep blue-violet band down the side of the window opening next to the wall. The upper two thirds of the canvas is done; the bottom third is bare white.

steps.name: Lay in the wooden sill

lays.what: the whole sill as a long rectangle for the top surface and a strip for the front edge along the bottom of the canvas, laid straight through where the blanket will sit

steps.after: The bottom third of the canvas is a flat warm red-brown sill from edge to edge, with no light or shadow yet. The whole canvas is now covered: window, wall and frame above, wood below.

steps.name: Shade the sill's front and the blanket's shadow

lays.what: a dark strip along the front edge at the very bottom, and a dark band across the sill where the blanket will sit and cast its shadow, darkest toward the right

steps.after: The sill now has a deep red-brown front edge along the bottom of the canvas and a dark band across its middle and right where the blanket will rest; the top of the sill at the left and the strip near the wall stay the warm mid brown.

steps.name: Lay the sun patches on the sill

lays.what: slanted patches of peach sunlight on the sill top at the left, under the window, with stripes of brown between them where the frame's shadow falls

steps.after: Bright slanted peach patches of sunlight lie on the left part of the sill, with warm brown stripes between them; the right of the sill and its front edge stay brown and dark. The background is finished; the cat and blanket are still to come.
steps.why: The sun patches tell the painter where the light comes from before the subject goes on.

steps.name: Build the blanket from rolls

lays.what: the folded blanket from simple pieces: one long flat oval ring across the sill, then a fat roll along its front edge and a second roll folded under it, with the back rim curving up on the right; laid straight through where the cat will lie

steps.after: A big flat mustard-yellow blanket now sits on the sill across the lower middle of the canvas: a wide oval with two rolls along its front and a raised rim at the right. It covers the area where the cat will go and has no shading or texture yet; the dark sill shows below and to the sides.

steps.name: Shade the blanket's folds

lays.what: deep ochre curved along the groove between the two rolls, the underside of the lower roll where it meets the sill, the right end, and a soft shadow inside the ring where the cat's body will rest

steps.after: The blanket now looks thick and round: honey-brown shadows curve under each roll, along the groove between them, at the right end, and in the hollow where the cat will lie. The tops of the rolls stay bright mustard.

steps.name: Press in the dark knit stitches

lays.what: rows of small slanted comma pairs, like a chain of Vs, following the curve of each roll over the whole visible blanket

steps.after: The blanket is covered in rows of small honey-brown V-shaped stitches that follow the curve of each roll, with mustard showing between them; it now reads as knitted but still looks a little flat and dull.
steps.why: Same mix as the folds, used right after while it is still fresh on the palette.

steps.name: Press in the sunlit stitches

lays.what: fewer, smaller pale yellow commas on the tops of the rolls and the left end facing the window, beside the dark stitches

steps.after: Pale yellow stitches catch the light along the tops of both rolls and the left end of the blanket, leaving the dark stitches and folds showing below them and at the right. The blanket is finished and the inside of the ring waits for the cat.

steps.name: Build the cat from simple shapes

lays.what: the whole curled cat in mid gray: a big oval for the body lying on the blanket, a circle for the head at its left end, two triangles for the ears, and a curved piece for the tail wrapped along the front, every stroke following the way the fur lies

steps.after: A flat mid-gray cat shape lies on the blanket: a large rounded body filling the middle of the canvas, a round head with two pointed ears at the left, and a tail curving along the front. No shading, white, stripes or face yet; the blanket shows around it.
steps.why: The light was stated at the start: from the window at the upper left. Every shadow and light on the cat keeps to that.

steps.name: Shade the cat's shadow side

lays.what: darker gray curved along the right side and bottom of the body, under the head and chin, and along the underside of the tail, leaving the mid gray on the top and left facing the window

steps.after: The cat now looks round: its far right side, its belly line and the underside of its tail and head are a darker gray, while the top of the back and head facing the window stay mid gray. Still no white, stripes or face.

steps.name: Paint the white muzzle, chest and paws

lays.what: the white muzzle and chin, the white blaze on the chest and shoulder, and the two front paws tucked under the chin as two rounded ovals, in two or three thin coats

steps.after: White fur now shows on the cat's muzzle and chin, a white blaze sweeps across its chest behind the head, and two plump white paws rest on the blanket under the chin. The rest of the cat is plain gray, shaded on the right.

steps.name: Pull the dark tabby stripes

lays.what: bold dark stripes curving around the body and over the back, bands across the tail, short lines on the forehead and cheeks, and the dark tips and backs of the ears

steps.after: The cat is now clearly a tabby: thick-to-thin charcoal stripes wrap around its body and back, the tail is banded, and fine stripes mark the forehead and cheeks. Gray shows between all stripes; the white patches stay clean. The ears are still gray inside.

steps.name: Paint the pink inside the ears

lays.what: the inside of both ears, one teardrop of pink in each triangle, leaving a gray rim around it

steps.after: Both ears now have soft pink insides framed by a gray and charcoal rim. The face is still blank: no eyes, nose or whiskers yet. The painting may look a little stiff and patchy here; that's normal.

steps.name: Flick in the silver fur

lays.what: short light flicks of silver gray all over the gray fur and across the edges of the stripes, following the way the fur lies around the body and out from the face, more on the top and left facing the window

steps.after: The cat's coat now looks furry: silver flicks soften every stripe edge and cover much of the top and left of the body and head, with the darker gray and charcoal still showing between them, especially on the shadowed right side.

steps.name: Flick the lit edge of the fur

lays.what: a few pale silver flicks only along the top edge of the head, the curve of the back, the top of the tail, and the edge of the white blaze, on the side facing the window

steps.after: A soft rim of light now runs along the top of the cat's head, back and tail, and the white blaze blends into the gray with feathery edges. The rest of the fur is unchanged and the face is still blank.

steps.name: Line the closed eyes and mouth

lays.what: the two closed eyes as short downward-curved dark lines, the small mouth line under the nose, and the little lines between the toes of both paws

steps.after: The cat now has two peaceful closed eyes curving down, a tiny mouth line in the white muzzle, and toe lines on both white paws. The nose and whiskers are still missing.

steps.name: Press in the pink nose

lays.what: the small triangular pink nose at the top of the white muzzle, between and below the eyes

steps.after: A small soft pink nose sits at the top of the white muzzle, and the face reads as a sleeping cat. Only the whiskers are still to come.
steps.why: Same salmon as the ears, mixed again in a small amount.

steps.name: Pull the white whiskers

lays.what: four or five thin white whiskers on each side, pulled out from the muzzle and lifted off: across the gray cheek to the left and over the chest to the right

steps.after: Fine white whiskers fan out from both sides of the muzzle across the gray fur and blanket edge. The painting is finished: a sleeping tabby curled on a knitted yellow blanket on a sunny sill by the window.
